Configure a trajectory study

cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration.Rd

Choose the observation cohort, state definitions and rules for a study. The analyst defines what each cohort means. This function creates the study folders and returns an environment used by getDataForStudy() and createTrajectories(). It does not import data or generate trajectories.

Usage

cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  cdm = NULL,
  studyName = "Cohort2Trajectory",
  baseUrl = "http://localhost:8080/WebAPI",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  atlasTargetCohort = NULL,
  atlasStateCohorts = NULL,
  stateCohortLabels = NULL,
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = NULL,
  stateCohortMandatory = NULL,
  stateCohortAbsorbing = NULL,
  stateSelectionType = NULL,
  oocFix = "None",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = NULL,
  outOfCohortAllowed = FALSE,
  runSavedStudy = FALSE,
  useCDM = TRUE,
  trajectoryDataObject = NULL,
  pathToData = "./Cohort2Trajectory/Data/importedData.csv",
  allowedStatesList = createStateList(stateCohortLabels),
  mergeStates = FALSE,
  batchSize = 1000,
  mergedStateOverrides = list()
)

Arguments

cdm

Not used by this function. Pass a connected CDMConnector object to getDataForStudy() and createTrajectories() when those steps use a CDM.

studyName

Study name, used as the folder name.

baseUrl

ATLAS WebAPI URL for cohort definitions. Use NULL to read local definitions from the study's JSON folder during import.

pathToStudy

Parent folder containing the study folder.

atlasTargetCohort

ATLAS ID of the target cohort. With baseUrl = NULL, supply its local JSON filename without the extension. The first target interval defines each patient's observation period.

atlasStateCohorts

ATLAS IDs of the state cohorts, in the same order as stateCohortLabels. With baseUrl = NULL, supply local JSON filenames without their extensions.

stateCohortLabels

Character vector of state labels. Supply one per state cohort for CDM input. Labels must be nonempty, non-missing and unique even when ignoring case. "0", "START", "EXIT" and "OUT OF COHORT" are reserved, including case variants. Labels may contain spaces or punctuation and need not start with a letter. They are separate from database cohort names and definition filenames.

stateCohortPriorityOrder

State labels from highest to lowest priority. All states within the observation bounds must be listed for discrete selection or continuous "Priority" selection. For a merged study, NULL uses a deterministic order of original states.

stateCohortMandatory

State labels that every included patient must have within the retained observation bounds. NULL or character(0) imposes no requirement. All labels are literal, including "No mandatory state". These requirements are applied during import. Rerun getDataForStudy() to change them.

stateCohortAbsorbing

State labels that end follow-up when selected. NULL or character(0) means none. For an unmerged study, use exact configured or observed labels, or a named discrete fallback. Configured states may be absent from the current data. For merged studies, supply original state labels here and use mergedStateOverrides for exceptions.

stateSelectionType

"First", "Overlap" or "Priority". Names ignore case and surrounding whitespace. NULL is allowed during configuration, but generation needs a choice.

oocFix

Discrete gap rule. "None" or "OUT OF COHORT" leaves an unresolved cycle. "Last present state" carries the last selected state forward when permitted. Any other nonempty, non-missing string names a fallback state. See the gap rules below.

trajectoryType

"Discrete" or "Continuous". Names ignore case and surrounding whitespace. NULL is allowed during configuration, but generation needs a choice.

lengthOfStay

Positive whole-number cycle length in days, within R's integer range. Required when generating discrete trajectories. It may be NULL during configuration. The final cycle is shortened at the observation boundary.

outOfCohortAllowed

Whether retained state records may extend the trajectory beyond the target interval's end. The target start is unchanged.

runSavedStudy

Set TRUE to restore the completed study from studyName/Settings/analysisSettings.rds. Supply its location and fresh input or connections, without repeating analytical settings.

useCDM

Whether to use a CDM for import and demographic joins during generation. Use FALSE for a local data frame or CSV.

trajectoryDataObject

Data frame for local input, with columns subject_id, cohort_definition_id, cohort_start_date and cohort_end_date. Use label "0" for observation intervals and the chosen state labels for state intervals.

pathToData

CSV path for local input when no data frame is configured. The CSV uses the same columns as trajectoryDataObject. Individual imports can select a different input through getDataForStudy().

allowedStatesList

Named list of allowed destinations, for example list(A = c("B", "C")). Source names must be unique, nonempty and non-missing. Put all destinations for one source in a single entry. An empty list allows all transitions. character(0) or NULL in an individual entry permits no destinations.

mergeStates

Set TRUE to represent overlapping state intervals as a combined state with explicit membership.

batchSize

Maximum patients per generation batch. Supply one positive whole number within R's integer range. The default is 1000.

mergedStateOverrides

List of mergedState() definitions. Requires mergeStates = TRUE. Supply at most one definition for each membership set. Omitted properties inherit from the original states.

Value

An environment containing the study settings.

Observation and state definitions

The target cohort supplies observation intervals. State cohorts describe events or periods within them, according to definitions chosen by the analyst. The first target interval for each patient sets the trajectory bounds, including for patients without state records.

Date intervals include both endpoints. A shared boundary date counts as one day of overlap. Discrete trajectories assign a state to each cycle. Continuous trajectories retain selected intervals and boundary markers without filling gaps or changing the times of simultaneous events.

State selection and gaps

In discrete trajectories, only overlapping states allowed from the last selected state compete. "First" chooses the earliest start. "Overlap" chooses the state covering the most distinct days in the cycle, combining repeated records without counting a day twice. "Priority" follows the supplied order. Ties use that order. Missing priority entries raise an error for all three discrete methods.

If no state qualifies, oocFix applies. Carry-forward needs an allowed self-transition, and a named fallback must be an allowed destination. Otherwise the cycle is "OUT OF COHORT". This label means no state was selected, not that observation ended. It preserves the last selected state for checking later transitions.

"None" and "Last present state" always select gap behaviour, even if a clinical state has that label. Fallbacks cannot be "0", "START" or "EXIT". Use the exact spelling of an existing state. A new fallback must not differ only in case from an existing state. For a merged state, use its display label, not its internal state_key. Text resembling a key can be a separate literal state if declared in stateCohortLabels.

Continuous "Priority" selection resolves overlaps among allowed states at each interval boundary. Every state within the bounds must appear in the priority order. An ongoing interval does not need a self-transition just because another record starts or ends. A selected absorbing interval keeps its bounded recorded endpoint even if a higher-priority record arrives later. Models requiring unique timestamps must resolve simultaneous events.

Transitions and absorbing states

Source names use exact state labels. Destination matching ignores case using R's locale-aware conversion. Output preserves the clinical labels. In an unmerged study with a nonempty rule list, an entry is required only when a state is used as a transition source. Rules apply separately to each patient and use the last retained clinical state.

A prohibited absorbing record does not end follow-up. Discrete generation ends after the selected absorbing cycle. Continuous generation ends at the retained absorbing interval's endpoint. Generation does not check outgoing transitions after a retained absorbing state.

Combining overlapping states

With mergeStates = TRUE, exact overlaps form combined states before discretisation. Membership is stored explicitly. Labels are never split to infer membership. A nonempty original-state rule list must include every original state. Use an empty list for unrestricted transitions.

Allowed destinations are inherited from the union of the source members' destinations. Each member newly added at the destination must be allowed by at least one source member. For a self-transition or a transition that only removes members, every retained destination member needs that permission.

A combination is absorbing if any member is absorbing. Its highest-priority member determines its priority. At equal priority, larger combinations come first, followed by state key order. Without a supplied priority order, original states are ordered deterministically. Explicit mergedState() properties replace the inherited properties. Absorbing status takes precedence over outgoing transitions.

The study environment's stateDictionary and the generated Data/stateDictionary.rds record the resolved states and their rules. See mergedState() for individual exceptions.

Saving and sharing a study

A completed import and generation saves the analysis settings in Settings/analysisSettings.rds. Only version 4 is accepted. Reconfigure and rerun older studies to create a current snapshot. CDM snapshots contain the exact cohort JSON definitions captured at import. Saved runs use those definitions and fresh patient data, leaving working JSON files unchanged.

Copy the completed study's Settings folder to the new location. Do not share Data, which contains patient records. Supply the new connection to import and generation, or configure fresh local input with useCDM = FALSE. Import must succeed before generation. To change definitions or analysis rules, configure a fresh study. Conflicting saved mandatory-state requirements also require a fresh run.

Local definition names may contain relative subpaths, such as states/A for JSON/states/A.json. Saved paths cannot be absolute or contain parent traversal.

Patient identifiers

IDs may be numeric whole numbers, character or integer64 values. Missing or blank identifiers are rejected. Temporary internal IDs are replaced by the original identifiers before output. For in-memory IDs at or above 2^53, use character or integer64 input to avoid rounded doubles.

See also

getDataForStudy, createTrajectories, mergedState

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "ExampleStudy",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = cohorts,
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("A", "B"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 7
)
} # }
